title: DcGvDkqioqS
adoptable: Treat one of the 3 point-slides as a literal before/after of the same artifact (same code or output evolving) instead of three unrelated points, so the video reads as one continuous "watch it get built/fixed" arc rather than a list.
Hold one visual significantly longer without cutting to create a "continuous build" feel, reserving fast punches only for the final payoff slide.

Pair the hook text with an immediate "before" visual on screen (rather than a text-only hook card) so the mismatch between the plain before-state and the promised result does the hooking work, not just the words.
End with a specific forward-looking tease ("next up: X topic") stacked right before the usual question/CTA, rather than the question alone.

title: Daa43CqoE_o
adoptable: Oversized 2-4 word headline card + one small supporting line underneath, held just long enough to read, before cutting to the next point (e.g. "Purity of Motion.", "Global Sound")
Continuous slide/fade/kinetic-type transitions between sections with zero hard cuts, instead of punch-cuts on every sentence
A short, clean closing card (logo/wordmark alone on a plain background) that holds for about a second right after the content ends, functioning as a visual full-stop before any CTA
A small rounded pill-shaped label used as a lightweight visual accent to flag the key takeaway of a text-heavy card (seen as "Go beyond" under the "Global Immersion" paragraph)

title: DdhR21VBfQH
adoptable: Front-load an explicit time/number promise in the hook and speak at a faster, denser pace than usual (this video: 17 words in the first 3s at 5.0 wps, vs our typical ~2.6 wps).
A deliberate near-silent beat right before a payoff number, timed to a visual (progress bar / counter) finishing.
Escalating proof structure across the body: claim → explanation → live demo with numbers → comparison → bigger demo → CTA, rather than three same-weight points.
Close on a text card that echoes the opening hook card's style/wording, bookending the video right before the CTA.
Let text-heavy screenshots (code, terminal, docs) carry their own on-screen text rather than stacking extra graphic highlight boxes over already-legible content.
